stops.s: The whole cell. Synthesis and secretion on the left, uptake and lysosomal traffic on the right. Gene names appear only where there is disease or APOE-dependent evidence.
APOE is inserted into the ER as it is translated. Alongside it the mevalonate enzymes end at DHCR24, which makes cholesterol from desmosterol. The first particle forms at the Golgi with ABCA1.

The vesicle fuses with the membrane and ABCA1 and ABCA7 lipidate APOE. Outside, particles carry APOC1, APOC2 and CLU/APOJ, and PLTP remodels them. Top left is an erythrocyte, the one intravascular compartment on this figure.
notes: The erythrocyte is here because the systemic genetics ties APOE lipoprotein handling to red cells: across ten lead variants in lipid-handling genes associated with red cell distribution width, the allele that raises HDL-C also raises RDW in nine of them — including SCARB1 and CD36, both already on the receptor list in this figure.

The route, from mouse genetics: in SR-BI-null mice raised HDL-C increases the erythrocyte cholesterol-to-phospholipid ratio, which lowers deformability and raises osmotic fragility, shortening lifespan and provoking a reticulocytosis — and a reticulocytosis is by construction a wider volume distribution. The red cell defect is markedly worse when APOE is deleted as well as SR-BI.

Only two receptors are drawn, and that is the point. A mature erythrocyte has no reactivity to lipid-free apolipoprotein; it is the standard negative control for receptor-mediated lipid efflux, so its sterol moves by non-specific exchange (t½ ≈ 3 h), which LCAT then makes net rather than merely balanced.

Compartment caveat: red cells are intravascular, whereas the rest of this cartoon is a brain cell. Brain APOE particles are astrocyte-derived and largely a separate pool from plasma — though lipid species do exchange at the CSF–blood barrier, with APOE genotype affecting that exchange in entorhinal cortex.
SR-BI and CD36 are coloured by this figure's code (APOE4-vs-APOE2 and Alzheimer genetics), not by their RDW direction.

stops.s: HSPG captures the particle and hands it to a receptor. Each receptor is filled with its evidence colour.
notes: The series above ranks the isoforms by LDLR affinity. APOE3 is the reference (Cys112, Arg158).
APOE2 is R158C (Arg158→Cys). APOE4 is C112R (Cys112→Arg).
E3-Cc is APOE3-Christchurch, R136S (Arg136→Ser), on an APOE3 backbone — a protective variant.
Residue numbers are for the mature protein; add 18 for precursor numbering.

stops.s: PICALM and BIN1 drive internalisation. The neck undergoes scission, then the coat uncoats. Cargo legend at top right.
notes: Therapeutic hypothesis 1 — an anti-APOE4 mAb, drawn ENGAGED rather than approaching: both paratopes on the particle surface, the Fc trailing, and the route to the clathrin pit dashed and barred. The intent is steric — occupy the APOE surface that HSPG and the LDLR family read, so the particle is never internalised.

It is a hypothesis, not a result: nothing in our data speaks to it, it must cross the blood-brain barrier or be given intrathecally, and isoform selectivity is unsolved — APOE3 and APOE4 differ by C112R, which is not surface-exposed on the lipidated particle.
E3-Cc is APOE3-Christchurch, R136S (Arg136→Ser), on an APOE3 backbone. APOE2 is R158C, APOE4 is C112R.
LDLR Kd on lipidated nanodiscs by SPR: E2 800 nM · E3 16 nM · E4 9 nM.
E3-Cc has no published Kd; it binds at 41% of E3 in a fibroblast assay.
The E4 step is ~1.8-fold by SPR, but runs with our finding that APOE4 lipoparticles accumulate intracellularly more than APOE3 — plausibly extra receptor engagement or slower recycling.

stops.s: Mildly acidic, and still holding APOE. A vesicle buds off to recycle receptors; the rest matures onward.

stops.t: Lipid and sterol catabolism, mTORC1 activation
stops.s: LIPA frees cholesterol from cholesteryl ester, and NPC2 with NPC1 export it at ER contact sites. TM6SF1 and SLC38A9 sense it and recruit mTORC1. Cholesterol and BMP rise here in APOE4. At left, a lysosome carrying undigested amyloid-β and tau heads for exocytosis.
notes: Therapeutic hypothesis 2 — the rapalog at right inhibits mTORC1 where cholesterol activates it on the lysosome. APOE4 glia hold 3× more lysosomal cholesterol, and TM6SF1 engages Ragulator cholesterol-dependently. But every gene in this module is transcriptionally flat, so the inhibitory bar is drawn on the pathway, not on our measurements.

LIPA carries a † because its blue comes from one ancestry stratum and reverses in the other: African-ancestry −0.61, European-ancestry +0.16, pooled −0.25 (between-stratum q 8.7e−8). “Lower in APOE4” is not supportable for LIPA as a general claim.
The lysosomal cholesterol machinery drawn here — NPC1, NPC2, TM6SF1, Ragulator, the Rag GTPases, mTORC1 — is transcriptionally flat: a lipid phenotype without a transcriptional signature.

stops.s: Less desmosterol leaves LXR/RXR on the LXR response element under-agonised, so the efflux programme falls.
notes: Therapeutic hypothesis 3 — chemical reprogramming, marked in the nucleus, is the only intervention on this figure aimed at cell state rather than at a single protein. Nothing in our data tests it: the label marks where such an intervention would act, not a result.

LXR agonism is pharmacologically responsive in APOE4 glia, even though no agonist is drawn: GW3965 and T0901317 restore APOE4 cholesterol efflux to untreated-APOE3 levels. The rescue is incomplete, and systemic LXR agonism drives hepatic lipogenesis.
Direct LXR/RXR targets down in human spatial transcriptomics data: PLTP −0.51, the APOE/APOC1/APOC2 cluster (−0.18, −0.75, −0.41), CD36 −0.92.
APOD is drawn uncoloured: it does NOT move in this pooled contrast, but within European-ancestry donors it is up +0.66, the 99.4th percentile of all genes.
ABCA1 and ABCA7 are flat in the spatial transcript data (FDR 0.13 and 0.70) but are decreased in isogenic APOE4 astrocytes.

stops.s: Synthesis to secretion to uptake to the lysosome, cholesterol back to the ER, and the response in the nucleus.
